sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header and project paths
sections.what: Documents how to run the importer and sets the project root folder used to find the input files.
sections.why: The header explains the dry-run default and the repeatable import design.
sections.watch_out: The root folder is worked out from this file's position, so moving the script breaks every default path.

sections.name: arg
sections.title: Command line path helper
sections.what: Reads an optional path flag for each input file, falling back to the default, and turns it into a full path. Also reads the commit flag.
sections.why: Lets a user point the importer at other files without editing the code.
sections.watch_out: A path flag given with no value after it may fail with an unclear error.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Load files and run the import
sections.what: Checks that every input file exists, parses them, prints counts, runs the import, then prints the summary and each refused value before closing the database connection.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the header.
sections.watch_out: Every file must exist before anything runs. The printed summary shows counts, while the reasons for individual refusals appear only in the refusal list.

summary: Command-line importer that loads the APS Reality Scan benchmark files (workbook and slide HTML, validation results, remote checks, and a data pack) into the evidence database. It runs as a dry run unless --commit is given.
purpose: Put the APS benchmark evidence into the evidence layer so values and their sources can be reviewed.
why: The header says re-running, or uploading the same files again, adds nothing because every record has a stable import key.
how: Works out the default file paths, checks that each file exists, parses the files, prints counts, and calls the importer with the commit flag. Then prints the summary and the list of refused values, and closes the database connection.
inputs: Five files: the data pack, workbench HTML, slide HTML, validation JSON, and remote results JSON. Each has a default path that can be overridden on the command line.
outputs: Database writes when committed. Console output with parse counts, a summary, and a list of refused values.
risks: With --commit it writes to the live database. A missing file stops the run before anything is written. Default paths point to attached asset folders, so moving files breaks the run.
debug: A 'file not found' error names the missing file. Compare the parsed counts in the first printed line against what you expect. Read the value refusals list to see why values were not imported.
